title: Company-wide policies and processes - access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Sofia Ramirez
body:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and our common internal templates. It is intended as the authoritative reference for employees, managers, and approvers.

Table of contents
1. Purpose and scope
2. Access & permissions
3. Change management
4. Data management
5. Procurement & expense policy
6. Vendor management
7. Travel policy and expense reimbursements
8. Internal templates and examples
9. Roles & ownership
10. Review cadence and exceptions

1. Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Provide clear, centralized policies to reduce operational risk, ensure compliance, and set consistent expectations for employees and contractors.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved third parties who access company systems or handle company data. Certain sections (e.g., vendor onboarding) include additional controls for Privileged or Regulated data.

2. Access & permissions
Intro: Access to systems and data follows the principle of least privilege. Requests are handled via the Access Request workflow in the IT ticketing system (see section 2.3).

2.1 Identity and authentication
- All employees must use corporate SSO (Okta) with MFA enabled.
- Password rotation is managed centrally; no local passwords should be stored or shared.

2.2 Role-based access control (RBAC)
- Access is granted by role where possible; role definitions live in /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth.
- Privileged roles (e.g., infra-admin, db-admin) require manager approval and a security reviewer.

2.3 Access request and approval flow
1. Open an Access Request ticket in our IT portal and select the target system.
2. Provide justification, duration (if temporary), and affected resources.
3. Manager approves for the employee; for contractor requests, the hiring manager must also confirm contract scope.
4. Security reviews requests for privileged data access.
5. IT implements and logs the change; the request auto-closes after verification.
- SLA: Standard access requests should be fulfilled within 3 business days; privileged requests within 5 business days.

2.4 Temporary access and emergency elevation
- Temporary access is granted with an expiration date (max 30 days) and must include re-validation by the manager.
- Emergency (break-glass) access requires an incident ticket and must be logged with justification; security performs post-hoc review within 3 business days.

2.5 Regular access reviews
- Quarterly access review conducted by team leads and security. Discrepancies must be remediated within 10 business days.

3. Change management
Intro: Change management ensures changes to production systems are planned, tested, and communicated. The process distinguishes between standard, minor, and major changes.

3.1 Change categories and definitions
- Standard change: Pre-approved low-risk change (e.g., routine config updates) - no CAB required.
- Minor change: Low-to-medium risk, requires peer review and notification to the on-call and platform team.
- Major change: High-risk or wide-impact changes (schema migration, runtime upgrades) - requires full change request, testing evidence, and CAB approval.

3.2 Change request process
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) through the Change Management tool with: summary, impact assessment, rollback plan, test results, deploy window, owner, and notified stakeholders.
2. For major changes, attach load and integration test results and a rollback checklist.
3. CAB (Change Advisory Board) reviews major changes at least 48 hours prior to the deploy window.
4. Post-deploy verification: owner performs smoke checks and updates CR status to 'validated' or 'rolled-back'.

3.3 Change windows, freeze periods, and exceptions
- Standard deploy windows: Mon-Fri 02:00-06:00 UTC for infra-affecting changes; application deploys follow team schedules.
- Code freeze applies to calendar days around major releases and quarterly financial close (schedule posted on the internal calendar).
- Emergency changes: Use the incident runbook flow; must be documented in the CR system within 24 hours.

3.4 Documentation and rollback
- Every change must have a rollback plan and owner. Rollback steps must be executable and tested in staging where possible.

4. Data management
Intro: Data handling policies ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of customer and company data. Applies to data at rest and in transit.

4.1 Data classification
- Public: Intended for public release.
- Internal: Company-internal information not intended for public disclosure.
- Confidential: Sensitive product, customer, or personal data; access restricted.
- Regulated: Data subject to regulatory controls (e.g., PHI, PCI, EU personal data).
- Classification tables maintained in /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention.

4.2 Data handling requirements by class
- Encryption: Confidential and Regulated data must be encrypted at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+, AES-256 or equivalent).
- Storage: Regulated data must be restricted to approved regions and infrastructure; approved storage locations are listed in the Data Residency doc.
- Sharing: Data sharing with third parties requires a DPA and security review.

4.3 Retention and disposal
- Retention periods set by data type; typical internal logs: 90 days, operational backups: 30 days, long-term analytics: 3 years (exceptions require legal approval).
- Secure deletion procedures: use approved wipe commands and document the deletion ticket.

4.4 Data access and audits
- All data access is logged. Security conducts periodic audit of access logs and anomalous activity.
- Data owners must respond to audit findings within the stated remediation SLA (15 business days).

4.5 Backups and disaster recovery
- Critical systems have daily backups with weekly snapshots retained for 30 days and monthly snapshots for 12 months where applicable.
- Restore drills should be performed quarterly for production-critical services.

5. Procurement & expense policy
Intro: Procurement balances speed and controls. This section defines thresholds, approvers, and required documentation for purchases and expense reimbursements.

5.1 Procurement thresholds and approvals
- Under $1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000- $10,000: Department head approval + procurement ops notification.
- $10,000- $100,000: Procurement ops approval + legal review for contract terms.
- > $100,000: Executive approval and finance & legal sign-off.

5.2 Vendor selection and competitive bidding
- For purchases > $25,000, procurement must obtain at least 3 competitive quotes unless a sole-source justification is approved.
- Preferred vendors list and contract templates reside in /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process.

5.3 Expense submission and reimbursements
- Employees must submit expenses via the corporate expense system within 30 days of incurring the expense. Receipts required for all items > $25.
- Per diem and travel allowances: domestic day rate $75, international rates vary by region (see Travel section).
- Reimbursement SLA: Finance processes standard reimbursements within 10 business days of submission (complete documentation).

5.4 Purchase orders and contract lifecycle
- All material purchases require a PO issued by Procurement.
- Contract lifecycle: request -> procurement negotiates -> legal reviews -> signatures via DocuSign -> contract recorded in CLM.

6. Vendor management
Intro: Vendors and third-parties introduce risk; this section sets the gating controls for onboarding, renewal, and offboarding.

6.1 Vendor onboarding checklist
- Business need documented and approved.
- Security review for data access and network connectivity.
- Contract with approved terms (DPA, security addendum if applicable).
- Procurement creates PO and vendor profile in the vendor management system.

6.2 Risk tiers and controls
- Low risk: SaaS tools with no access to confidential data - standard contract.
- Medium risk: Vendors with operational data or limited access to internal systems - require security questionnaire and periodic reviews.
- High risk: Vendors handling regulated or customer data - require on-site audits or SOC2 report, legal & security sign-off, and technical isolation.

6.3 Renewal and offboarding
- Renewals reviewed 60 days before expiry; security and procurement review compliance posture.
- Offboarding: revoke credentials, remove network access, confirm data return or secure deletion, and close the vendor account in the vendor registry.

7. Travel policy and expense reimbursements
7.1 Booking and approvals
- Business travel must be pre-approved by the manager. For international travel, travel clearance and insurance verification required.
- Use approved travel vendors for booking; exceptions must be justified in the expense submission.

7.2 Per diems and allowable expenses
- Domestic: $75/day (meals & incidental).
- International: region-specific per diems published on the Travel page.
- Allowable expenses: reasonable airfare (economy unless approved), lodging (standard business class), ground transportation, business meals. Personal expenses are not reimbursable.

7.3 Non-reimbursable items and fraud prevention
- Non-reimbursable: minibar, personal entertainment, spouse travel (unless pre-approved).
- Suspected fraud triggers a finance & people-ops review and may escalate to disciplinary action.

8. Internal templates and examples
- Access Request template (copy into IT portal): Title, Requestor, Target System, Justification, Duration, Manager Approval, Security Reviewer.
- Change Request checklist: Summary, Impact, Backout Plan, Test Evidence, Stakeholders, Deploy Window, Post-deploy Verification.
- Vendor Onboarding form: Business Owner, Vendor Name, Data Access Required, Contract Term, Security Questionnaire link, PO number.
- Expense submission checklist: Trip dates, purpose, receipts attached, account code, manager approval.

Example: Expense submission minimal checklist
- Employee name
- Trip dates and purpose
- Total amount claimed
- Itemized receipts (attached)
- Cost center and account code
- Manager approval signature or approval ID

9. Roles & ownership
- People Ops: overall owner for policies, training, and travel administration.
- Security: owns access policy enforcement, RBAC definitions, audits, and vendor security reviews.
- Procurement & Finance: owns procurement thresholds, PO issuance, vendor payments, and contract lifecycle.
- IT/Platform: implements access, change processes, and ensures logging and monitoring.
- Team leads: approve access and expenses for their direct reports.

10. Review cadence and exceptions
- Policy review: Annual full review by People Ops, Security, and Finance; interim updates as regulatory or operational needs change.
- Exceptions: Must be documented and approved by the policy owner and the relevant stakeholder (security/legal/finance). Exceptions are recorded in the Exceptions register and reviewed quarterly.

Appendices
A. Escalation contacts
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security: security@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Finance: finance@redwood.ai
- IT Support: it-support@redwood.ai

B. TL;DR quick reference (one-page)
- Access: request via IT portal; least privilege; quarterly reviews.
- Changes: CRs for major changes; CAB approval required.
- Data: classify and encrypt; follow retention schedule.
- Procurement: follow thresholds; PO required.
- Vendors: onboard with security review and contract.
- Travel: pre-approve, submit receipts within 30 days.
